title: Pirates Resisted An Attempt To Search Their Junk By The Packet Boat Of The Customs Cruiser Chuen Tiad J. Kondrup, Morpeth, Miao Fu

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPALITY
C. & S. B. REGISTR.
N. D 3718.
Dte 7/6/32

Sensational Tale Of Sea
Terrorists Revealed By
Inquest On Pirate Victims

A sensational chapter was added yesterday to the annals of piracy in Chinese waters in the Nantao District Court.

Inquest into circumstances surrounding the slaughter of one foreign and two Chinese customs officials as well as one other Chinese before the machine guns of pirates last Thursday off Woosung brought to light the existence of a huge band of sea terrorists, whose depredations outrank those of any other known bandit organization in recent local history.

Four Chinese, who had been held prisoner aboard the pirate sloop, testified to a record of piracy and murder on the high seas, climaxing in open warfare with customs officials. Their account put to shame the atrocities of local land bandits of the last decade. Reports of the inquest were given this paper by a court attendant.

Four Witnesses Talk

The four witnesses were brought to Shanghai on Sunday aboard the customs cruiser, Lu Hsing, which had spent two days combing the waters and surrounding land areas of Woosung in attempts to trace the pirate junk. The quartet stated that they had been held aboard the junk against their will. They related the following story:

About a week ago, the four together with about 10 others had been anchored off Sukiang, intending to come into Shanghai with the high tide. A huge five masted sailing ship under full canvas suddenly bore down upon them. The appearance of the vessel corresponded with the description of a well-known pirate ship that for months has been preying on small craft in the Sukiang region; so without asking questions the master hove weighed anchor and gave the wind every inch of canvas in his efforts to make land before being overtaken by the pirate ship.

Pirated Fire

The five-masted vessel bore down on the fleeing craft and fired a discharge of six rifle shots at it, passing the ship and its crew unscathed except for one forward shot. One of the shots splintered the main mast of the junk, and as fly of the rigging fell it was observed that the sails were torn.

Immediately after boarding the junk, the leader of the pirates called for the two men in charge of the junk; and when they responded both were shot dead. Their bodies were hurled over the side into the sea.

Ship Rifled

The bandits then took everything of value, including $2,000 cash and deposited it aboard their ship. The pirate chief then ordered the junk to return to Sukiang for $6,000 ransom upon receipt of which he would return the captured junk and crew to the owners. Thirty heavily armed pirates were sent to accompany the junk and six members of the crew back to Sukiang. The pirate ship then pulled away, and nothing has been seen or heard of it since.

A hasty trip was made to Sukiang, and without difficulty the ransom money was secured. The trip was begun back to the pirate ship. En route two fishing junks were held up. Five men aboard the junks were killed, and two wounded were thrown over the side into the sea.

One small fishing boat was set aside for ransom money with eight armed pirates aboard it.

Junk Overtaken

On Thursday morning, at daybreak the junk sighted the pirate launch from the customs cruiser Chuenchio. All sail was hoisted and the junk headed out to sea, but it was overtaken after a short run by the customs power boat. Manifest papers were signalled for, and when the original manifest of the pirates were ordered to board a whale-boat and present the papers, which they did.

Although the "papers" were in order, Customs Officer J. Koudring, Danish, became suspicious of the junk, and he ordered two of his men to search it. As the two men stepped aboard the launch, the pirate leader drew a revolver and shot one of the customs officers through the head killing him instantly. The other five leaped from their sampan into the water, and swam themselves behind the small craft from the junk.

上海公共租界
刑事与特别课登记处
编号 D 3718。
日期 1932年6月7日

海盗受害者死因研讯揭露海上恐怖分子惊人内幕

昨日，在南市地方法院，中国水域海盗史册上又增添了惊人的一章。

针对上周四在吴淞口外，一名外籍及两名华籍海关官员以及另一名华人在海盗机枪下惨遭杀害一案的情况进行的死因研讯，揭示了一个庞大的海上恐怖团伙的存在，其暴行之烈，超过了近期本地历史上任何已知的匪帮组织。

四名曾被囚禁在海盗单桅帆船上的华人作证，陈述了该团伙在公海上的海盗行径和谋杀记录，最终以与海关官员的公开武装冲突达到高潮。他们的供述使过去十年间本地陆上土匪的暴行相形见绌。本报从一名法庭侍役处获得了此次死因研讯的报告。

四名证人陈述

这四名证人于周日由海关巡舰“卢兴”号（Lu Hsing）带至上海，该舰曾花费两天时间搜寻吴淞水域及周边陆地，试图追踪那艘海盗舢板。这四人称他们是被迫扣留在该船上的。他们讲述了如下经过：

大约一周前，他们四人连同其他约十人停泊在苏疆（Sukiang，音译）附近，打算趁涨潮进入上海。一艘张满帆的巨大五桅帆船突然向他们逼近。该船的外观符合数月来在苏疆地区掠夺小型船只的一艘著名海盗船的描述；因此，船长未加询问便起锚，并张开所有风帆，竭力在被海盗船追上之前靠岸。

海盗开火

那艘五桅船向逃跑的船只逼近，并向其发射了六发步枪子弹，除了一发击中船头外，船只及其船员均安然无恙。其中一发子弹击碎了舢板的主桅，随着索具落下，人们观察到船帆已被撕裂。

海盗登上舢板后，其头目立即传唤负责该船的两名男子；当两人回应时，当即被枪杀。他们的尸体被抛入海中。

船只遭劫

匪徒随后洗劫了所有值钱物品，包括2,000美元现金，并将其运上他们的船只。海盗头目随即命令该舢板返回苏疆索取6,000美元赎金，声称收到赎金后将把被扣的舢板和船员归还给船主。三十名全副武装的海盗被派往护送该舢板及六名船员返回苏疆。随后海盗船驶离，此后便再无其踪迹或消息。

一行人匆忙赶往苏疆，毫不费力地筹得了赎金。随后开始返回海盗船所在处。途中拦截了两艘渔船。渔船上的五人被杀，两名伤者被抛入海中。

一艘小渔船被留出用于运送赎金，船上有八名武装海盗。

舢板被追上

周四清晨破晓时分，该舢板发现了来自海关巡舰“川乔”号（Chuenchio）的海盗汽艇。舢板升起所有风帆并向外海驶去，但不久便被海关摩托艇追上。信号要求出示舱单文件，当原本的海盗被命令登上捕鲸船并提交文件时，他们照办了。

尽管“文件”看似合规，丹麦籍海关官员 J. Koudring 对该舢板产生了怀疑，并命令手下两人进行搜索。当这两人踏上汽艇时，海盗头目拔出手枪，击中一名海关官员头部，致其当场死亡。其余五人从他们的舢板跳入水中，游到那艘来自海盗大船的较小船只后方躲避。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, JUNE 4, 1932
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL
C. & S. B. REGIST.
No. D 3718.
Date 7-6-32.

Pirates Led By Men In
Uniform Used Automatic
Rifles In Yangtze Fight

Another Of Customs Crew Dies; Picket Boat's
Battle Scarred Appearance; First Officer's
Miraculous Escape; Eye-Witness Accounts

ENCOUNTER TOOK PLACE IN SHALLOW
WATER; OFFICERS USE LEWIS GUN

The death roll in the battle between the Customs crew
and pirates in the Yangtze Kiang estuary on Thursday
morning, has now amounted to four on the side of the
officials. Yesterday, one of the Chinese, who was wounded
on the Customs picket boat, or pinnace, died at the Lester
Hospital from wounds. An examination yesterday showed
that the picket boat was riddled above the water line with
bullets, and authentic reports from eye witnesses show that
the pirates were directed by men in uniform and that they
used Thompson automatic rifles. The pinnace men replied
with their arms and a Lewis gun, and it is believed that the
losses among the pirates may be heavy, as several of them
were in a sampan and caught between two fires. The late
Mr. J. Kondrup, third officer, was hit by two bullets in the
stomach and Mr. Morpeth, the first officer, had his holster
ripped, also his sleeve, by bullets. But he was unscathed.
The search for the junk has proved fruitless.

Hanging from the davits as
mute testimony of the dastardly
attack that was made upon its
crew early on Thursday morning,
the picket boat of the Customs
cruiser Chuentiao is in need of a
few minor repairs. Bullet holes
mark its starboard side and inside
the little craft the wood is splint-
ered badly.
The Chuentiao is back in Shang-
hai harbour following an unsuc-
cessful search for the junk on
which the Chinese pirates hid and
opened fire on the Customs offi-
cers on Thursday. Life on the
smart little cruiser is not the
same as before. J. Kondrup the
third officer, who died from a
stomach wound during the early
morning battle, was a popular
official, and his presence is being
sadly missed by the many for-
eigners and Chinese that make
up the complement of the cruiser.
Eye-witness stories of the battle
with the pirates present many
fresh points, chief of which is that
the pirates used Thompson
automatic rifles, while the picket
boat crew fought back with a
Lewis gun. Pirates wearing uni-
forms and stripes on their arms,
gave directions aboard the
junk, which was a big three-
masted, sea-going vessel. Evid-
ently these men were either dis-
banded soldiery or regular band-
its.

Bullet Holes On Belt
Besides the pinnace, with its
bullet-scarred side, there are other
tokens of the battle aboard the
cruiser. For instance there is an
officer's belt with leather wallet
attached. One bullet has pierced
the wallet and another smashed
through the belt. Both these
marks are at spots where the
wallet would rest against the
stomach. Kondrup fell half over
the pinnace when hit and his
body slid to death.
Attached to the same belt with
leather wallet attached so on
was a memorandum of the battle.
This belt and holster belongs to
the first officer, J. R. Morpeth,
who went through the action
unscathed. Yet his holster has
been torn by a bullet and his
sleeve was also ripped by
a bullet. He was

Authentic reports of the pirate
battle reveal that the Chuentiao
was cruising 80 miles off Woosung
and along the Yangtze Kiang
estuary, when a big junk was
picked out for examination. As
the junk was moving along in
shallow water, the Chuentiao
lowered its pinnace, the small boat
being manned by the first and
third officers, a foreign boat ex-
aminer, a Chinese third class
tide waiter and ten armed Chinese.

Sampan Approaches
As the pinnace approached the
junk, a sampan with six men
aboard left the old fashioned
craft and came towards the
launch. The men aboard the
sampan carried the junk's papers
and these appeared to be in
order. However, the mysterious
appearance of the junk caused the
Customs officers to decide to board
and examine her.
With the sampan in tow, the
pinnace moved alongside the junk
and without any warning the
pirates opened fire. They em-
ployed automatic rifles and spray-
ed the little boat with bullets.
The pirates had the advantage of
firing from above while the men
aboard the pinnace had to fire
upwards at assailants, who for
the most part, were under cover.
Six men went down on the pin-
nace, while the sampan, caught
between two fires, suffered casual-
ties.
The heavy wooden sides of the
junk absorbed the bullets from
the Lewis gun but the pinnace
was shot about and a score of
wounds dotted her side. The boat
examiner had his cap shot off.
The dastardly and sudden attack
completely disorganised the Cus-
toms boat, which was forced to
move off. The junk also moved
away and was soon lost to sight
in the haze.

Pinnace Is Shambles
The pinnace had left the
Chuentiao at 9.25 a.m. with a
cheery crew aboard, she returned
two hours later and resembled a
shambles. Three dead and three
wounded lay about the decks. The
scene that presented itself was a
shock to the remaining officers on
the Chuentiao. The commander,
three engineer officers had re-
mained on board, and although
they had seen the pinnace and
the junk in the distance no sound
of the firing had reached them.
However, they immediately made
arrangements for the comfort of
the wounded men, and after the
bodies of the dead and the injur-
ed had been transferred to an-
other Customs vessel, they com-
menced their search for the junk.
This search proved unavailing,
and although the officers obtained
further information regarding the
junk, they were forced through
fog, to commence the return
journey to Shanghai on Thursday
afternoon.
A number of bullets have been
extracted from the wooden sides
of the pinnace, and they appear
to be a little larger than revolver
bullets.

Death Of Chinese
One of the three Chinese
Customs men to be shot down in
the engagement, died of wounds
in the Lester Hospital yesterday
at 2.50 p.m. He had been badly
injured and little hope was held
out for him when he was brought
ashore on Thursday night. His
name was Miao Fu, and although
operated upon, he failed to sur-
vive. The other wounded men—
both Chinese—are progressing.
One was hit in the stomach and,
following an operation, is doing
well, while the other man is not
in a serious condition, having been
hit in the leg.

Inquest Yesterday
Yesterday afternoon at 3 o'clock,
inquests were held on the body of
J. Kondrup, the Danish officer to
be shot by the pirates, and also
on the bodies of the two Chinese
who were shot outright on the
pinnace.

Funeral To-day
To-day the funeral will be held

《上海泰晤士报》，1932年6月4日，星期六
上海公共租界
刑事与特别课登记处
编号 D 3718。
日期 1932年6月7日。

身穿制服者率领海盗
在长江交火中使用自动步枪

又一名海关船员身亡；巡逻艇战痕累累；
大副奇迹般生还；目击者叙述

交火发生在浅水区；官员使用刘易斯机枪

周四早晨在长江口发生的海关船员与海盗之间的战斗，目前官方方面的死亡人数已达四人。昨日，一名在海关巡逻艇（或称小艇）上受伤的华人，因伤势过重在莱斯特医院（Lester Hospital）去世。昨日的检查显示，巡逻艇水线以上部分布满弹孔，来自目击者的可靠报告表明，海盗由身穿制服的人员指挥，并使用了汤普森自动步枪。小艇船员使用随身武器和一挺刘易斯机枪进行还击，据信海盗伤亡惨重，因为他们中有几人位于一艘舢板上，陷入两面夹击。已故的三副 J. Kondrup 腹部中两弹，大副 Morpeth 先生的枪套和袖子也被子弹击穿。但他本人毫发无伤。对那艘舢板的搜寻至今未果。

悬挂在吊艇架上的海关巡舰“川乔”号（Chuentiao）的巡逻艇，无声地见证了周四清晨对其船员进行的卑鄙袭击，目前需要进行一些 minor 维修。弹孔标记了其右舷，在这艘小船内部，木材严重碎裂。

“川乔”号在周四对藏匿中国海盗并向海关官员开火的舢板进行 unsuccessful 搜寻后，已返回上海港。在这艘精致的小巡舰上，生活已非往昔。在三副 J. Kondrup 于清晨战斗中因腹部枪伤去世后，这位颇受欢迎的官员的离去，令组成该巡舰编制的外籍和华人同仁深感悲痛。

关于与海盗战斗的目击者叙述提供了许多新细节，主要一点是海盗使用了汤普森自动步枪，而巡逻艇船员则用刘易斯机枪还击。身穿制服、臂戴袖章的海盗在那艘大型三桅海船上发号施令。显然，这些人要么是遣散的士兵，要么是职业匪徒。

腰带上的弹孔

除了侧面布满弹痕的巡逻艇外，巡舰上还有其他战斗的痕迹。例如，有一条附有皮夹的军官腰带。一颗子弹穿透了皮夹，另一颗击穿了腰带。这两处痕迹都位于皮夹紧贴腹部的位置。Kondrup 中弹时半身探出巡逻艇外，身体滑落身亡。

同一条附有皮夹的腰带上还别着一份战斗备忘录。这条腰带和枪套属于大副 J. R. Morpeth，他在行动中毫发无伤。然而，他的枪套被一颗子弹撕裂，袖子也被一颗子弹划破。他是

关于海盗战斗的可靠报告揭示，“川乔”号当时正在吴淞外80英里处及长江口沿线巡航，此时选中一艘大型舢板进行检查。由于该舢板在浅水区行驶，“川乔”号放下了巡逻艇，小艇由大副和三副、一名外籍验船师、一名华籍三等看潮员以及十名武装华人驾驶。

舢板靠近

当巡逻艇接近舢板时，一艘载有六人的舢板离开那艘老式船只，向巡逻艇驶来。舢板上的人携带着那艘大舢板的文件，这些文件看起来合规。然而，那艘大舢板的神秘外观促使海关官员决定登船检查。

巡逻艇拖着那艘小舢板，靠上大舢板，海盗在未发出任何警告的情况下开火。他们使用自动步枪，向小船扫射。海盗占据从高处射击的优势，而巡逻艇上的人不得不向上方射击，且袭击者大多有掩护。巡逻艇上有六人倒下，而那艘小舢板因陷入两面夹击也遭受了伤亡。

大舢板厚重的木质船侧吸收了刘易斯机枪的子弹，但巡逻艇遭到射击，侧面布满了约二十处伤痕。验船师的帽子被击飞。这次卑鄙且突然的袭击完全打乱了海关船只的阵脚，迫使其撤离。那艘大舢板也随即驶离，很快消失在薄雾中。

巡逻艇一片狼藉

巡逻艇于上午9点25分离开“川乔”号时，船员们情绪高昂，两小时后返回时却宛如屠宰场。甲板上躺着三具尸体和三名伤者。这一幕令“川乔”号上剩余的官员震惊。指挥官和三名轮机官留在舰上，虽然他们在远处看到了巡逻艇和大舢板，但未听到枪声。然而，他们立即着手安排伤员的救治，在将死者和伤者转移至另一艘海关船只后，他们开始搜寻那艘大舢板。

此次搜寻证明无效，尽管官员们获得了关于那艘大舢板的进一步信息，但由于大雾，他们被迫于周四下午开始返回上海的行程。

从巡逻艇的木质船侧取出了数颗子弹，它们看起来比左轮手枪子弹稍大。

华人死亡

在此次交火中被枪击的三名华籍海关人员之一，于昨日下午2点50分在莱斯特医院因伤去世。他在周四晚被送上岸时伤势严重，生还希望渺茫。他名叫缪富（Miao Fu，音译），虽经手术，仍未能幸存。其他两名伤者——均为华人——情况好转。一人腹部中弹，手术后恢复良好，另一人腿部中弹，情况不严重。

昨日死因研讯

昨日下午3时，对被海盗枪杀的丹麦籍官员 J. Kondrup 的遗体，以及在巡逻艇上被当场枪杀的两名华人的遗体，进行了死因研讯。

今日葬礼

今日将举行葬礼

(C. & S.B.) Office Notes

D. C. (Crime)

Date June 4, 1932.
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL P...
C. & S. B. REGISTER.
No. D 3718.
Date 6 / 6 / 32.

I beg to attach translations of a bloodstained
log book and documents handed to me at 11 a.m., June 3,
by Mr. Skuse, Chief Tidesurveyor, Chinese Maritime
Customs, Shanghai, for purposes of examination in
connection with the murder of Customs Cruiser officers
and crew by an armed junk at Woosung on June 2, 1932.
The book was found in the possession of a foreign
officer who was shot and killed whilst examining same.

Copies of translations of the documents and
the originals have been forwarded to Mr. Skuse and
the information contained therein has enabled the
Customs Authorities to identify the junk responsible
for the outrage and necessary action is being taken
by them.

It is evident that the junk was carrying
contraband cargo when held up for examination by the
Customs Authorities.

A bullet found in the Customs boat was also
handed in for examination and is being dealt with
by the Arms Identification Section.

C.P.

（刑事与特别课）办公室笔记

犯罪科

日期 1932年6月4日。
上海公共租界警务处...
刑事与特别课登记处。
编号 D 3718。
日期 1932年6月6日。

兹附上由上海中国海关总看潮员 Skuse 先生于6月3日上午11时交给我的沾血日志簿及文件的译文，以供审查，此事涉及1932年6月2日在吴淞口，海关巡舰官员及船员被武装舢板谋杀一案。

该日志簿是在一名外籍官员身上发现的，该官员在检查该船时被枪杀。

文件译文副本及原件已送交 Skuse 先生，其中包含的信息使海关当局得以识别应对此暴行负责的舢板，他们正在采取必要行动。

显然，该舢板在被海关当局拦截检查时，正载有违禁货物。

TRANSLATION

The log-book is hereby issued by the Fokien
Customs subject to the following regulations governing
any junk or boat sailing between Foochow and other
ports after it is duly registered and branded.
(1) Subsequent to the issue of the log book, it shall
be kept on the junk or boat to which it is issued and
is not transferable and no alterations shall be made
therein/ The junk or boat loading cargo/sailing between
Foochow and other ports, either import or export, the
logbook is to be produced for the examination of the
Custom Officers.
(2) License shall be liable to punishment for illegally
unloading, provided that the particulars of goods and
date are specified in the logbook, between one port to
another, until it reaches its destination when it is
found without being checked by the Customs authorities
between the two ports stated therein. The same rules
are applicable for export.
(3) Usual fee is to be charged for re-issue when a
logbook is lost without sufficient reason.
(4) In case of any change of the boat or Captain (owner
of the boat) the log book together with other documents
are to be produced to the Customs where it will be
dealt with according to usual procedure.
(5) Logbook is issued free of charge nor is there any
fee for its renewal.

本航海日志由福建海关签发，受以下规章约束：凡在福州与其他港口之间航行的任何民船或船只，经正式注册并烙印后，须遵守这些规定。
(1) 航海日志签发后，应保存在其所签发的民船或船只上，不得转让，也不得在其中进行任何涂改。装载货物、在福州与其他港口之间航行（无论是进口还是出口）的民船或船只，须出示航海日志供海关官员查验。

(3) 若航海日志无正当理由丢失，补办时需收取常规费用。
(4) 若船只或船长（船主）发生变更，须将航海日志及其他文件提交海关，海关将按常规程序处理。

BOAT LICENCE.

With a view to the enforcement of maritime
regulations governing contrabands and to the prevention
of piracy all boats (or junks), large and small, for
fishing as well as for commerce, running along the coast
of the Fokien Province, are required to apply to the
authorities of the district concerned for registration
and the issue of a licence, before they can be allowed
to pass.

This licence is issued to:-
Kyung Foong Zung (金豐順), owner of the boat
for commerce.
Yue Tai Shing (游泰興), guarantor.
Crossbeam: 18' 8".
Sailors: 15 persons.
Fee: $23.40.
Registration No. 2380.
Date: May 17, 21st year of
the Republic (1932).

Regulations.

1. The licensee is not allowed to smuggle contrabands nor
to hide pirates.
2. The licensee is required to have the licence renewed
at the end of each season in each year.
3. The licensee is required to report to the Customs
Authorities of the port which the boat passes for
examination and permission to pass.
4. The licensee is required to furnish the measurement
of the crossbeam and the number of sailors.
5. The licensee, when wishing to sail to another port,
is required to present this licence (to the Authorities
concerned) for examination and registration.
6. The licensee is required to pay licence fees at the time
of the issue or renewal of the licence.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, JUNE 3, 1932
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTR.
No. D 27/8.
Date 6 / 6 / 32.

Pirates' Broadside Rakes
Customs Picket Boat Fore
And Aft In Deadly Battle

MURDEROUS AND SUDDEN FIRE FOLLOWS
ATTEMPTED SEARCH OF MYSTERIOUS
JUNK YESTERDAY BY OFFICIALS

FOREIGN OFFICER, FIVE CHINESE, SHOT
DOWN BY FIRST PIRATE VOLLEY

Three Dead, Three Wounded, On Customs Boat; One
Pirate Killed; Foreigner Dies Outright; Junk
Not Yet Captured By Searchers

Rifles and revolvers rattled through the haze on the Yellow Sea yesterday morning as a terrific and murderous broadside from a pirates' junk raked the decks of a Customs picket boat, and cut down nearly all her crew, causing instant death to a foreign officer, two Chinese, and wounds to three other Chinese. With the control of the small boat disorganized, and the officers laying either dead or seriously wounded on the decks, the remaining Customs crew swung around their machine gun and with the first traverse brought down one of the pirates. Other pirates probably died too, but in the smoky haze the pirate junk slipped away and fled for safety. The encounter followed the attempted search of the junk off Woosung by the crew of the picket boat, which was attached to the Customs cruiser Chuentiao. The pirates are still at large. The bodies of the dead men and the wounded were brought back to Shanghai last night. The three Chinese wounded are now in the Lester Hospital, two of them being in a serious condition.

On Wednesday afternoon late, the Chuentiao slipped down-river as she had done on many occasions before. The Chuentiao is a Customs Revenue cruiser, and the trim little craft is the pride of all who work aboard her. Probably on Wednesday the crew again looked forward to just one such day as had passed on previous occasions. Little of note would occupy their attention. But in reality death lay in store for a number of them.

The Chuentiao stood off the river and cruised through the muddy waters; Woosung lay away to westward. The boat moved within the 12 mile limit of Chinese territorial waters. Old fashioned Chinese junks swayed by sluggishly towards the shore. The Chuentiao slowed down, her officers and crew had much work to do among the junks. Permits had to be demanded and examined. Sometimes these examinations yield excellent results, for the Woosung shore abounds in pirates and is the hitching place for smugglers.

The Search
It was nearing 4.30 yesterday morning when the Chuentiao lowered her smart looking picket boat. The Chinese sailors went aboard and so did J. Kondrup, third officer, a foreigner of Danish extraction. The search commenced. One by one the junks came under the critical eyes of the customs officials. Quite a number of them had already been looked over and papers examined, when a heavy old junk attracted the attention of the crew of the picket boat. The picket boat swung around and made for the junk. Away in the distance lay the Chuentiao, partly obscured by the haze.

Investigations commenced. As the picket boat came alongside the mysterious looking old craft, one of the junk's crew volunteered to come aboard the picket boat. He did not exactly fill requirements. A search of the junk was imperative. Probably the search would prove very interesting. The officer intimated his intentions and he and his crew prepared to board the junk.

Murderous Attack
Without the slightest warning the pirates opened fire. There was a blaze of fire from the junk and down in a heap went a number of the picket boat's crew. Kondrup was one of the first to fall. He was struck in the pit of the stomach and died almost immediately. Another Chinese Customs officer went down dead, a bullet in the head. One of the sailors on the picket boat also fell dead, shot through the head. Three other Chinese on the picket boat fell wounded.

Recovering from the surprise the remaining crew of the picket boat answered the fire and brought their machine gun into action. They accounted for the pirate who had presented the suspicious papers. He fell dead on the picket boat. Probably some of his confederates went to their doom too, on the junk. She was riddled with the machine gun bullets. But the haze saved her. Assisted by the bad visibility, she moved away and before the Chuentiao could come up to the scene of the action, the junk had disappeared. Completely disorganized by the effect of the sudden and dastardly attack, the survivors aboard the picket boat were unable at the moment to initiate the chase after the disappearing junk.

Search Continues
The Chuentiao is still searching for the pirates; there seems little doubt that the native craft is manned by piratical Chinese. The work of bringing in the dead and the wounded was left to the Haihsing, which arrived in Shanghai harbour at 8.15 last night.

The three Chinese who were still living were taken to the Chinese Lester Hospital and by 11 o'clock last night two of them were in the operating theatre. One was suffering from a stomach wound, and another from serious wounds that have placed his life in danger. The third Chinese suffers from a leg wound and late last night he was reported to be sleeping peacefully.

The body of the pirate is now at the Chinese mortuary while the bodies of the foreigners and of the dead Chinese of the picket boat are lying at the International Funeral Parlour. An inquest on the cases will probably be opened today.

《字林西报》，1932 年 6 月 3 日，星期五
上海公共租界工部局警务处
刑事与特别课 登记
编号 D 27/8。
日期 32 年 6 月 6 日。

海盗舷侧齐射扫荡
海关缉私艇首尾
陷入殊死战斗

谋杀性且突然的火力紧随
官员昨日试图搜查神秘民船之后

一名外籍警官、五名中国人，在海盗第一轮齐射中倒下

海关艇上三人死亡，三人受伤；一名海盗被击毙；外国人当场死亡；搜查人员尚未抓获民船

昨天早晨，黄海上迷雾弥漫，随着海盗民船猛烈且致命的舷侧齐射扫过海关缉私艇的甲板，步枪和左轮手枪声大作，几乎击倒了艇上全体船员，导致一名外籍警官和两名中国人当场死亡，另外三名中国人受伤。由于小艇的控制陷入混乱，军官们或死或重伤躺在甲板上，剩余的海关船员转动机枪，第一次扫射就击倒了一名海盗。其他海盗可能也丧生了，但在烟雾弥漫的 haze 中，海盗民船溜走并逃往安全地带。此次遭遇战发生在隶属海关巡舰“泉钓”号（Chuentiao）的缉私艇船员试图在吴淞附近搜查该民船之后。海盗目前仍在逃。死者遗体和伤者已于昨晚被带回上海。三名受伤的中国人的现在莱斯特医院（Lester Hospital），其中两人情况严重。

周三下午晚些时候，“泉钓”号顺流而下，正如它以前多次做过的那样。“泉钓”号是一艘海关缉私巡舰，这艘整洁的小船是船上所有工作人员的骄傲。也许在周三，船员们再次期待着像以往那样平淡的一天。没有什么值得注意的事情会占据他们的注意力。但实际上，死亡正等待着他们中的许多人。

“泉钓”号停在河口外，在浑浊的水域中巡航；吴淞位于西方远处。船只在中国领海 12 海里界限内移动。老式的中国民船懒洋洋地摇向岸边。“泉钓”号减速，其军官和船员在民船间有许多工作要做。必须索要并检查许可证。有时这些检查会产生极好的结果，因为吴淞沿岸海盗众多，也是走私者的聚集地。

搜查
昨天凌晨接近 4:30 时，“泉钓”号放下了外观漂亮的缉私艇。中国水手登艇，丹麦裔外籍三等官 J. Kondrup 也登艇。搜查开始。一艘又一艘民船接受了海关官员的审视。相当数量的民船已经被查看过，文件也已检查，此时一艘沉重的老旧民船引起了缉私艇船员的注意。缉私艇调头驶向该民船。远处，“泉钓”号部分被薄雾遮蔽。

调查开始。当缉私艇靠近那艘看起来神秘的老旧船只时，民船的一名船员自愿登上缉私艇。他并不完全符合要求。对民船的搜查势在必行。这次搜查可能会非常有趣。警官表明了意图，他和他的船员准备登船。

谋杀性袭击
海盗在没有丝毫警告的情况下开火。民船上一片火光，缉私艇上的多名船员倒成一堆。Kondrup 是最早倒下的人之一。他被击中腹部，几乎立即死亡。另一名中国海关官员头部中弹，当场身亡。缉私艇上的一名水手也头部中弹倒地身亡。缉私艇上另有三名中国人受伤倒下。

从震惊中恢复过来后，缉私艇剩余的船员还击，并将机枪投入战斗。他们击毙了那名出示可疑文件的海盗。他倒在缉私艇上身亡。他在民船上的同伙中可能也有一些人丧命。民船被机枪子弹打得千疮百孔。但薄雾救了它。在能见度不良的协助下，它移开，在“泉钓”号赶到行动现场之前，民船已消失无踪。缉私艇上的幸存者因突然且卑鄙的袭击而完全陷入混乱，当时无法发起对消失民船的追击。

搜查继续
“泉钓”号仍在搜寻海盗；毫无疑问，这艘本土船只由从事海盗活动的中国人驾驶。运送死者和伤者的工作留给了“海兴”号（Haihsing），该船于昨晚 8:15 抵达上海港。

三名尚存活的中国人被送往中国莱斯特医院，到昨晚 11 点，其中两人已在手术室。一人腹部受伤，另一人伤势严重，生命垂危。第三名中国人腿部受伤，昨晚深夜据报道正在安睡。

海盗的尸体现在停放在中国殡仪馆，而外籍人士和缉私艇上死亡中国人的尸体则停放在国际殡仪馆。对这些案件的验尸讯问可能今天开始。
